newsitem.title: JAPAN: Bank of Kinki to write off 20 bln yen bad loans.
newsitem.headline: Bank of Kinki to write off 20 bln yen bad loans.

text.p: Bank of Kinki Ltd said on Monday it would write off about 20 billion yen worth of problem loans in 1996/97, ending on March 31.
The bank said in a statement it expects problems loans as of the end of March to be around 82 billion yen, down from 90 billion yen a year ago.

Of the total, loans to bankrupt clients are expected to total about 26 billion yen, and loans whose interest payments have been in arrears for more than six month are expected to total around 56 billion yen, it said.
The bank's capital adequacy ratio is expected to be about 4.4 percent as of the end of 1996/97.
In conjunction with the revision in its earnings forecast, the company announced several restructuring measures.
Bank of Kinki said it would cut its work force by 4.3 percent in the next two years, and executive bonuses would not be paid, the statement said.
Executive salaries would be frozen and may also be cut, the statement said.
The company also hopes to raise 45 billion yen from the sale of land.
